cultural.vision_reason: Classic Baule wooden "asye usu" bush-spirit figure, seated on a stool with characteristic coiffure, scarification, and beaded anklets — a well-known Baule genre with strong internal attribution ("Baule-style carver").

physical.title: Male Figure from a Pair (asye usu)
physical.medium_raw: Wood, resin, glass beads, plant fiber, and metal
physical.summary: Baule figures carved as pairs usually represent untamed spirits of the wilderness called asye usu. These spirits may intervene in the lives of individuals by taking possession of them. If this possession does not result in madness, it can lead to the human host’s becoming a diviner who can enter into a trance to reveal the causes of ailments and other misfortunes. People who feel their lives are being interrupted by the asye usu commission carvings representing idealized male and female forms whose grace and beauty in both anatomy and adornment will seduce the spirits and compel them to use the sculptures as their temporary homes.

location.made_in_place: Africa, West Africa, Côte d’Ivoire, Baule-style carver
